prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures a downward-angled living room layout, separating the near foreground on the lower left (a guitar and dark clutter pile at ~0.5–1.2 m, within arm's reach and partly cropped at the frame edge) and bottom-right ottoman (~1 m, partly out of view) from the mid-ground carpet (~1.5–2.5 m), the couch, end table, and coffee table (~2.5–3.5 m), and the recessed hallway behind them (>4 m). A brown-and-white dog stands on the floor in front of the camera wearer at ~1.2–1.5 m in frames 1–3, facing and looking up toward the camera wearer, while a second dark-furred animal lies on the floor ~0.8–1 m behind it (~2–2.5 m from the camera wearer) next to a blue cloth. Across frames 1–5, the camera wearer turns slightly downward and left while the brown-and-white dog approaches into arm's reach (<0.8 m) and exits the bottom edge by frame 5, uncovering the lying animal behind it. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clarifies the 3D geometry and distance of the shadowed dark clutter on the left and the dark lying animal against the floor. However, it is unreliable where it completely misses the camera wearer's motion-blurred hands reaching out (<0.5 m) at the bottom of frame 2, merges the coffee table's thin legs with the floor, and washes out the dog's head at the bottom edge of frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map tracks several foreground and mid-ground regions across the 5 frames, detecting the standing brown-and-white dog (~1.2–1.5 m away, facing and looking toward the camera wearer) in frames 2–3 and the dark animal lying behind it (~2–2.5 m away, oriented to the right) as a dog in frame 4 and overlapping cat/dog masks in frame 5 after the first dog walks forward out of the lower frame. Relative to the dog in frames 2–3, a large teal mask on the right (~1.5–3 m away, below the coffee table) and brown/pink/cyan masks on the left (~0.5–1.5 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach and partly occluded by the left and bottom borders) bracket the center floor space. The map helps isolate the dark lying animal in frames 4–5 from the shadowed carpet and adjacent clutter, which is hard to distinguish in the RGB image alone. However, the map is highly unreliable in its class labels and completeness: no other people are present in the scene, yet it misclassifies the left-side guitar stand, bags, and the camera wearer's blurry left hand (<0.5 m in frame 2) as one or two 'person' instances in frames 2–5, mislabels the patterned rug as a 'couch' in frames 2–3, and mislabels a dark blanket on the actual couch (~3 m away) as a 'cat' in frame 1. It also fails to segment the standing dog in frames 1 and 4–5, as well as the actual white couch, coffee table, and ottoman.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders yellow body skeletons only in frames 1 and 2 and contains no detections in frames 3–5, even as the camera shifts slightly downward and the foreground dog approaches the camera wearer. In reality, no visible people are in front of the camera wearer—only the camera wearer's own hands appear briefly within arm's reach (<0.5 m) at the bottom of frame 2, while the two animals occupy the center floor (~1.2–2.5 m away). Instead of tracking real bodies or hands, the pose map places a false skeleton in frame 1 on the dark throw blanket draped over the white couch (~3 m away, above and behind the standing dog, oriented sideways toward the left) and another in frame 2 on the end table and couch armrest (~2.5–3 m away, oriented as if facing the camera wearer with an extended right arm). Nothing in the pose map adds valid spatial detail beyond what is visible in RGB, and it is completely unreliable here because it hallucinates human keypoints on mid-ground furniture and blankets while missing the camera wearer's actual hands in frame 2.
